sources.journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
money: AcknowledgementsThe authors thank the members of the SSG (Cees van Leeuwen, Tomas Palenicek, Rudy Schreiber) for evaluating the safety data and providing advice.

design.quote: The current, first-in-human study (N = 14) assessed the impact of three escalating doses of 3-MMC (25, 50 and 100 mg) on vital signs, neurocognitive function, state of consciousness, appetite and drug desire
design.text: a first-in-human, cross-over, placebo-controlled trial of 3-MMC in 14 participants

findings.quote: The generalizability of the safety and tolerability profile of 3-MMC as observed in the present trial should be further evaluated in clinical trials that include larger samples and repeated dosing.
findings.text: The safety and tolerability profile of 3-MMC needs further evaluation in clinical trials that include repeated dosing.

findings.quote: Abuse liability after (repeated) use of high doses of 3-MMC has not been systematically studied in humans but preclinical evidence has suggested addictive properties of 3-MMC
findings.text: Abuse liability after repeated use of high doses of 3-MMC has not been systematically studied in humans, though preclinical evidence suggests addictive properties.

limits.quote: Furthermore, carry-over effects between treatments cannot be entirely excluded, given that cathinones and 5HT2A agonist may induce changes in neuroplasticity that may outlast a wash-out period of 7 days.
limits.text: Carry-over effects between treatments cannot be entirely excluded because cathinones may induce changes in neuroplasticity that last longer than 7 days.
